title: A scammer targeted my little brother's first legendary (Part 1)
caption: Part 2 tomorrow. What should I do to him? (fictional story)
text: A scammer tricked my seven year old brother out of his first legendary pet, so I made him a promise. I'd get it back. My brother Max saved for three months for a Shadow Dragon. Three months of chores. Taking out trash. Folding towels. Every Robux he earned went into one pet. The day he got it, he carried my phone around the house to show everyone. Even the dog. Two days later, he came into my room crying so hard he couldn't talk. A player named LuckyGifts_77 told him there was a new update. If you put a legendary in a trade and the other person accepts with nothing, the pet turns mega neon. Max believed him. Why wouldn't he? He's seven. He put the Shadow Dragon in. LuckyGifts accepted. And left. I checked his profile. Joined three days ago. Forty two friends. All little kids. All with the same story in their comments. He scammed me too. Where's my pet. Please give it back. He'd been doing it all week. To kids. So I made an account. I named it SmolBunny2018. I put on a bunny costume, the pink one, and I typed slowly with spelling mistakes. Then I joined his server and walked around holding the best pet I own. A mega neon Frost Dragon. It took him four minutes to find me. He typed, hey cutie, wanna see a cool trick? I typed back, yes pleeease. Part two is on my page tomorrow. Follow so you don't miss it.

title: A scammer targeted my little brother's first legendary (Part 2)
caption: Was this fair? Be honest (fictional story)
text: The scammer who took my little brother's Shadow Dragon thought he'd found his next easy target, and he walked right into it. If you missed part one, a player named LuckyGifts_77 had been scamming little kids all week, so I made a fake little kid account to catch him. He told me the same lie. Put your Frost Dragon in, accept with nothing, and it turns mega. I typed, ok but I'm scared, you go first so I can see. He laughed. He typed, fine, watch. And to prove the trick was real, he put a pet in his own side of the trade. Max's Shadow Dragon. He thought I'd decline. Kids always decline. I didn't. I accepted. Instantly. He typed, wait, no. Then he typed, that's not how it works. Then nothing for a whole minute. Then, give it back or I'll report you. I typed, for what? I followed your trick. And I left. I gave the Shadow Dragon back to Max that night. He hugged the computer. Actually hugged the screen. Then I did one more thing. I took screenshots of all forty two kids in his friend list, every comment, every message he sent them, and I sent them all to Roblox. A week later his account was gone. Banned. Max asked me how I got his dragon back. I told him I traded for it. Which is technically true. Would you have done the same?

title: A Brookhaven player knew which school I go to (Part 1)
caption: Part 2 tomorrow. How did they know? (fictional story)
text: A player in Brookhaven parked outside my house and said the name of my real school. I'd never told anyone online where I go. It started on a Tuesday. I was decorating my Brookhaven house, normal stuff, and a school bus pulled up in front of my driveway. Just sitting there. Engine running. Nobody got out. The driver's name was a string of numbers. I typed, can I help you? They typed back, you're going to be late. I laughed. It was nine at night. I logged off. Wednesday, the bus was there again. Same spot. This time they typed, you forgot your math homework again. I froze. Because I had. My teacher literally said that to me in class that morning. Word for word. You forgot your math homework again. I told myself it was a coincidence. Teachers say that to everyone. Thursday, I joined a new server. Fresh server. Different house. I waited ten minutes. Nothing. I started to relax. Then the bus pulled up. Same numbers. And on the side of the bus, someone had used the paint tool to write three words. The name of my school. Not a nearby school. Not a guess. My school. With the mascot. A blue hawk. I looked out my real window. There's a bus stop across the street from my house. And somebody was sitting at it. At ten p.m. On their phone. Part two is on my page tomorrow. Follow so you don't miss it.

title: A Brookhaven player knew which school I go to (Part 2)
caption: Did you guess who it was? (fictional story)
text: The player stalking me in Brookhaven was sitting at the bus stop across my real street, and I went outside to see who it was. If you missed part one, someone kept parking a school bus outside my Brookhaven house, quoting my teacher, and painting my school's name on the side. I grabbed a flashlight. My heart was pounding so hard I could hear it. I opened the front door. The person at the bus stop looked up. And waved. It was my neighbor, Ethan. He's in my grade. Different class. He held up his phone. Brookhaven. The bus. I walked over and said, are you serious? He said, bro, I've been trying to get you to notice me for a week. He'd moved in two weeks earlier. He sat behind me in math, which is how he knew about my homework. He saw my username on my laptop screen. He wanted to ask if I'd play with him, but he said it felt weird to just walk up. So he figured the bus thing was a cool way to introduce himself. A cool way. I told him it was the scariest thing that had ever happened to me. He looked so embarrassed. He said, sorry, I thought you'd think it was funny. And honestly? Now I kind of do. We play every night now. He still drives the bus. Every time I log in, it's parked in front of my house. He says it's tradition. Would you have gone outside?

title: My Grow a Garden neighbor sold me a fake seed (Part 1)
caption: Part 2 tomorrow. What would you plant? (fictional story)
text: My neighbor in Grow a Garden sold me a seed he said was legendary, and it grew into a single weed. I'd been saving all week. Every carrot. Every strawberry. Every blueberry bush I watered at two a.m. before school. I had almost a million coins. And the guy in the plot next to mine, Farmer_Jake, kept walking past my garden saying the same thing. I've got a secret seed. Only one in the server. Grows the rarest fruit in the game. He showed me a picture. Glowing purple fruit. Gold leaves. I'd never seen anything like it. He said, nine hundred thousand. Final offer. I paid. He handed me the seed. I planted it in the middle of my garden, right where everyone could see. I watered it. I waited. I watched it grow for an hour. A weed. A tiny, brown, crispy weed. I checked the picture again. Zoomed in. Somebody had edited it. Badly. The gold leaves were just yellow highlighter. I went over to his plot. He'd already left the server. With my nine hundred thousand coins. But he forgot one thing. His garden was still there. Grow a Garden saves your plot. And I knew exactly when his crops would be ripe. Because I'd been watching him water them every night. For a week. Right next to me. Tomorrow at six a.m., they'd be ready to harvest. Part two is on my page tomorrow. Follow so you don't miss it.

title: My Grow a Garden neighbor sold me a fake seed (Part 2)
caption: Was this too far? Be honest (fictional story)
text: Farmer Jake took nine hundred thousand coins for a fake seed, so I set my alarm for six a.m. If you missed part one, my Grow a Garden neighbor sold me a legendary seed that turned out to be a weed, then logged off with all my coins. I knew his crops would be ripe at six. What he didn't know is that when you leave a server, your garden doesn't follow you. It stays. And in Grow a Garden, anyone can pick fruit from a garden if the owner isn't there to stop them. I logged in at five fifty eight. His plot was still next to mine. Full. Every plant glowing. Six o'clock hit. I started picking. Dragonfruit. Mangoes. Coconuts. Grape after grape after grape. I filled my whole inventory, ran to the shop, sold everything, ran back, and did it again. Seven trips. At six forty, he logged in. He walked over to his empty garden. He typed, what happened. I typed, I don't know, maybe it was a weed. Then I planted the weed right in the middle of his plot. He didn't type anything for a long time. Then he typed, how much did you get? I checked. One point two million coins. Three hundred thousand more than he stole. He typed, that's actually fair. Then he asked if I wanted to start a farm together. I said no. Would you trust Farmer Jake?

title: My cousin ate my Kitsune fruit as a prank
caption: Who's the worst cousin you know? (fictional story)
text: My nine year old cousin ate the rarest fruit I've ever found in Blox Fruits, and he did it on purpose. I'd been grinding for a month. Sea events. Raids. Getting destroyed by people way higher level than me. Then one night, under a random tree on the second sea, I found it. Kitsune. The fox fruit. Worth more than my entire account. I stored it immediately. I didn't even tell my friends. I told one person. My cousin Leo. Because he was sitting right next to me at my grandma's house, and I literally screamed. The next morning, I logged in and my storage was empty. I checked my character. My character was a fox. A giant glowing blue fox. I hadn't eaten anything. Then I heard giggling from the couch. Leo had my login saved on his tablet from last summer. He'd logged in at six a.m., pulled the Kitsune out, and eaten it. On my account. As a prank. He said, now you're a fox. You're welcome. I almost cried. Then I tried it. One move. The whole island lit up blue. Players flew off the map. Somebody typed, what is THAT. I won every fight that day. Every single one. I bountied up more in one hour than in the whole month before. I went back to the couch. I said, I'm not mad. He said, I know. I'm the best cousin. I said, change my password though. Would you have forgiven him?

title: My dad joined Dress to Impress and won every round
caption: Should he do a fashion show next? (fictional story)
text: My dad played Dress to Impress for the first time, and he won every single round. I'm still not okay. It started because I needed one more player for a private server. My friends were offline. My dad was on the couch. I said, dad, just stand in the corner, you don't have to try. He said, what's the theme? I said, it doesn't matter. He said, it always matters. First theme. Beach day. Everyone made bikinis and sunglasses. My dad made a lifeguard. Red shorts. Whistle. A tiny sunburn he drew on with the makeup tool. He got five stars from everyone. Second theme. Royalty. Everyone made a crown and a ball gown. My dad made a king who just woke up. Crown slightly crooked. Bathrobe. Holding a coffee mug. The whole server lost it. Third theme. Villain. He made a tax collector. Suit. Clipboard. Little glasses. Stars everywhere. By round six, people were joining just to see what he'd make. Someone asked if he had a TikTok. Someone asked if he was a famous designer. He typed back, I'm a dad. I sell insurance. That's the round he won with a bee costume for the theme Insurance Fraud. I don't even know how that was a theme. He played for three hours. Then he got up, said, that was fun, and went back to the couch like nothing happened. He hasn't played since. He says he doesn't want to ruin his record. Could your dad do this?

title: I was murderer five rounds in a row and nobody believed me
caption: Has this ever happened to you? (fictional story)
text: I got murderer five rounds in a row in MM2, and nobody believed me even when I told them. Round one. I got murderer. Normal. I won. Round two. Murderer again. Okay, lucky. Somebody typed, sus, same guy twice. Round three. Murderer. I didn't even try to hide. I just walked up to people. They kept saying, no way it's him again, it's random. Round four. Murderer. At this point, I'm feeling bad. So I typed in chat, I'm the murderer, just so you know. Everyone laughed. Someone typed, nice try, sheriff. The sheriff didn't even look at me. He shot a girl named PinkBubble instead. She typed, why. I won round four. Round five. I got murderer again. I couldn't believe it. So I did something insane. I took the knife out. In the lobby. Just held it in my hand and walked around. Nobody ran. Someone typed, he's trolling, he's probably innocent, ignore him. The sheriff walked right up next to me. Stood there. I typed, bro, I'm holding a knife. He typed, that's a skin. It wasn't a skin. I won round five. After the round, the sheriff added me as a friend. He typed, okay you were actually the murderer that whole time. I typed, I told you. He typed, I thought you were a really good liar. I typed, I didn't lie once. Have you ever told the truth and nobody believed you?

title: Someone kept stealing my brainrots, so I built a trap base
caption: Would you have fallen for it? (fictional story)
text: Someone stole my brainrots three nights in a row in Steal a Brainrot, so on night four I built a base that was all trap. The first night, I lost two. The second night, four. The third night, the thief took my best one. My Tralalero. I'd had him since my first day. Every time, the same player. A guy named Speedy_Stealer. And every time, he left a message in chat. Ty for the brainrot, noob. So I watched him. He always came at the same time, right after my base lock ran out. He always came through the front. He always grabbed the most expensive brainrot first. So I rebuilt my whole base around one idea. The most expensive brainrot I owned went right at the back. Right behind the door. And in front of it, I put twenty of the cheapest brainrots in the game. All lined up. Shiny. Loud. Very grabbable. And I waited by the door with my bat. Night four. Lock ran out. Speedy came running in. Right on time. He grabbed the first cheap one. Then the second. Then he saw the line. All twenty. He couldn't help himself. He kept grabbing. One by one. Slower and slower. By the time he reached the back, he was carrying so many he could barely move. That's when I closed the door. And swung. He dropped everything. All twenty. Plus my Tralalero, which he'd stolen the night before. It came back home. Then I typed, ty for the brainrot, noob. Would you have fallen for it?

title: A level one noob saved my Jailbreak bank robbery
caption: Do you help noobs? Be honest (fictional story)
text: I tried to rob the bank in Jailbreak with a level one noob, and he's the reason I didn't go to jail. I was alone. Every robbery that night, I got arrested. Bank, arrested. Museum, arrested. So when a player named Dino_Kid_9 asked, can I come with you, I almost said no. Default avatar. No car. Level one. But he looked so excited. So I said, sure, stay close. We drove to the bank in my car. Inside, I got the money. He just stood there. Walked into a laser. Got stuck behind a door. I had to go back for him twice. Then we heard sirens. Three cops. Right outside. I knew it was over. I typed, run. Then I noticed. Dino_Kid wasn't running. He was standing in the corner, completely still. The cops ran in. They ran right past him. Straight to me. One of them reached for his handcuffs. And then, out of nowhere, Dino_Kid_9 jumped out from behind the cop and grabbed the cop's keycard. And then he opened the side door. The one you need a keycard for. The one I didn't even know existed. He typed, this way. We ran out the side, into the sewer, and came out three streets away. Free. Full money bag. I typed, how did you know about that door? He typed, I watched a video. I've been studying for a month. I just never had anyone to play with. He's my robbery partner now. He's level forty. Do you help noobs?

title: In Doors, room 50 had a note with my username on it
caption: Would you have opened it? (fictional story)
text: In Doors, I found a note in room fifty with my username written on it, and I was playing solo. I play Doors alone a lot. I like the quiet. I know every room. I know where Rush comes from. I know when to hide. So when I walked into the library at door fifty, I knew exactly where the hint papers would be. But on the desk, the one right by the entrance, there was a new paper. White. Folded. I'd never seen it there before. I picked it up. On the front, in handwriting, it said my username. All of it. With the numbers. I opened it. Inside, one sentence. Don't hide in the third closet. I laughed. I thought it was some kind of update. A new feature. I kept going. Fifty one. Fifty two. Then the lights flickered. Rush was coming. The closest closet was the third one in the hallway. My hand was already on the key. I remembered the note. I ran past it. Hid in the fourth. Rush went by. And when I came out, the third closet was open. Not broken. Open. And there was something standing inside it. Not a monster from the game. A player. Default avatar. No name over their head. Facing the back wall. I left the game. I checked my recent players list. The only name in it was mine. Twice. Would you have hidden in the third closet?

title: My Brookhaven house got robbed by a six year old with a plan
caption: Should I hire him? (fictional story)
text: A six year old robbed my Brookhaven house, and honestly, his plan was better than anything I've ever done in that game. I was in my kitchen, making fake pancakes. A little kid knocked on my door. Tiny avatar. Dinosaur hat. He typed, hi, can I use your bathroom. In Brookhaven, you don't need a bathroom. I said, sure. He walked in. Went upstairs. Three minutes later, he came back down, said, thank you, and left. That's when I noticed my TV was gone. Then my couch. Then my car wasn't in the driveway. I ran outside. He was driving my car down the street with my couch strapped on top. Wait, you can't strap a couch on a car in Brookhaven. He'd figured out how. I don't know how. I chased him. He went straight to his house, two streets away. And it was full. My TV. My couch. Somebody's fridge. Somebody else's piano. Seven beds. He'd robbed the whole neighborhood. One bathroom visit at a time. I knocked on his door. He opened it. He typed, hi. I said, that's my couch. He said, no, it's my couch now. Do you want it back? I said, yes. He said, okay, you have to pay rent. I asked how much. He said, a hug emote. I did the emote. He gave me my couch back. Then he asked if he could use my bathroom again. Would you let him in?

title: A girl traded her whole inventory for my plain dog. Here's why.
caption: Would you have taken the trade? (fictional story)
text: A girl in Adopt Me offered her entire inventory for my plain, normal dog, and when I asked why, I almost cried. The dog was nothing special. Not neon. Not mega. Just a basic brown dog I got from a starter egg two years ago. I named him Biscuit. He's level max because I take him everywhere. So when a player named StarryNight_Lily sent me a trade with three legendaries, a mega neon owl, and a ride potion, for Biscuit, I declined. I thought it was a mistake. She sent it again. And again. I typed, are you sure? This dog is worth like nothing. She typed, I know. Please. I asked why. She didn't answer for a while. Then she typed something I'll never forget. My real dog was named Biscuit. He was brown. He died last month. I've been looking for a brown dog named Biscuit in every server. Yours is the first one. I didn't know what to say. I sat there for a minute. Then I declined her trade. And sent her my own. Biscuit, for nothing. She typed, no, I have to give you something. I said, you can give me one thing. Promise you'll take him everywhere. She accepted. A week later, I found her in a server. Biscuit was following her. Wearing a tiny crown. She'd given him the best accessory in her inventory. She waved. I waved back. Would you have taken her trade?

title: One jump from the top of Tower of Hell, my mom unplugged the router
caption: Has your mom ever done this? (fictional story)
text: I was one jump away from beating Tower of Hell for the first time ever, and my mom unplugged the router. Let me explain how much this meant. I'd been trying for nine months. Nine. I'd made it to the last floor four times and fallen every single time. My friends had all beaten it. I was the only one left. This night, everything was perfect. The tower was easy. The timer had four minutes left. I cleared the spinning floor. I cleared the tiny beams. I was on the last section. The finish was right in front of me. One jump. My hand was shaking. I lined it up. And the screen froze. Reconnecting. I sat there, staring at it. Reconnecting. Then from the hallway, I hear my mom. Okay, everybody, screens off, dinner time. She'd unplugged it. The whole router. For dinner. I walked into the kitchen like I'd seen a ghost. She said, what's wrong with you? I said, nothing. I just lost nine months of my life. She said, it's a video game. I said, it was one jump. She said, then you'll do it again. And here's the thing. After dinner, I got back on. I beat it on the first try. First try. Maybe I needed the break. Maybe the pasta helped. I'm still not telling her she was right. Has your mom ever done this to you?

title: My grandma's Grow a Garden is worth more than my house
caption: Could your grandma do this? (fictional story)
text: My grandma has been playing Grow a Garden for two weeks, and her garden is worth more than everything I own in Roblox combined. It started when I showed her the game on my tablet. I thought she'd think it was boring. She said, oh, it's just like my real garden. Can I try? I made her an account. Username, GrandmaRoses. Then I went to school. When I came home, she'd planted forty carrots in perfect rows. Perfect. Same distance apart. She said, carrots like space. I laughed. The next day, she'd sold all the carrots and bought blueberry bushes. The day after, strawberries. Then she started waking up at five a.m. to water. She told me plants grow better in the morning. That's not how the game works. But her plants were growing faster than mine. By day ten, she had a dragonfruit tree. By day twelve, she had six. People started visiting her garden. Just to walk around in it. She'd put little benches between the rows. A tiny pond. A sign that said, please don't pick, this is grandma's garden. Nobody picked. Not one player. Yesterday, she showed me her coins. Forty two million. I have three hundred thousand. She asked if I wanted to borrow some. I said no. I have my pride. Then I asked how much interest. She said, call me more often. Could your grandma do this?

title: I hatched a Huge on my birthday and a scammer showed up in minutes
caption: What would you have done? (fictional story)
text: I hatched my first Huge pet in Pet Simulator on my birthday, and a scammer showed up in less than five minutes. I'd been hatching for a year. A whole year. My mom let me stay up late because it was my birthday, and at eleven fifty nine, I opened one last egg. Huge. Gold. Glowing. My whole screen exploded with confetti. Everyone in the server could see it. That was the problem. A minute later, a player named Official_Mod_Team messaged me. Congrats on your huge. To keep it safe, we need to verify it. Send it to our verification account and we'll send it right back with a badge. I knew it was a scam. Everyone knows. But I wanted to see how far he'd go. So I typed, wow, thank you. How does it work? He sent me a link. I didn't click it. He sent me a trade instead. I put in a pet. Not my Huge. A tiny, level one cat I'd named Huge Cat. Huge. Cat. And I sent it. He accepted in half a second. Then he typed, wait, what is this. I typed, it's my huge. He typed, this is a cat. I typed, a huge cat. He blocked me. I unblocked myself by joining his server, and I sat next to him with my real Huge for twenty minutes. Didn't say anything. Just sat there. Glowing. He left. Best birthday ever. Would you have done the same?

title: A player in 99 Nights kept saying don't light the fire
caption: Would you have lit it? (fictional story)
text: On night forty in 99 Nights in the Forest, a player joined our server and told us not to light the campfire. We'd been playing together for weeks. Me and three friends. We had a system. Wood before dark. Fire at sunset. Never leave the light. That's the one rule everyone knows. So when this new player walked out of the trees, no name, gray avatar, and stood next to our fire pit, we thought it was a noob. He typed, don't light it tonight. My friend Jayden laughed. He typed back, we'll die if we don't. The player typed, you'll die if you do. Then he walked back into the trees. It got dark. We stood there, wood in our hands, looking at each other. The deer started making noises. Closer. Jayden said, he's trolling, light it. I did. The fire lit up the whole camp. And in the light, I could see them. Standing at the edge of the trees. Not one deer. Dozens. Standing still. Watching the fire. They'd never been there before. The fire had never brought them. The fire had always kept them away. Then the gray player typed in chat, one word. Run. We ran. Away from the fire. Into the dark. Everything behind us went quiet. We survived the night. In the morning, our camp was gone. Just the fire pit. Still burning. Would you have lit the fire?

title: My teacher was secretly the best player in our school's Roblox game
caption: Would you want your teacher in your server? (fictional story)
text: Somebody in my class made a Roblox game of our school, and the best player in it turned out to be our math teacher. The game was simple. It was our school, built pretty badly, and you had to race from your locker to class before the bell. My friend Marcus made it. Everyone in our grade played. And at the top of the leaderboard, by a lot, was a player called SquareRoot_Wizard. Nobody knew who it was. His times were insane. He knew every shortcut. He went through the cafeteria window. Nobody even knew that window opened. Marcus didn't even know. He built the game. We started talking about it in class. Who's SquareRoot Wizard? Is it a high schooler? Is it someone's brother? And the whole time, Mr. Patel was at the front of the room, writing equations on the board, not saying anything. Then one Friday, he handed back our tests. And at the bottom of mine, in red pen, he'd written, nice try on the cafeteria shortcut. You're still two seconds slow. I looked up. He was smiling. The whole class figured it out at the same time. Somebody yelled, no way. He said, back to fractions, please. But that weekend, the whole class tried to beat his time. Nobody did. Monday morning, his time was even faster. He'd improved it. On Sunday. Would you want your teacher in your server?

title: I got a job at the Bloxburg pizza place, and my boss was my dad
caption: Would you work for your dad? (fictional story)
text: I got a job at the pizza place in Bloxburg, and my manager turned out to be my dad. I had no idea he even played. It was a private roleplay server. Some guy was running the pizza shop like a real business. Shifts. Uniforms. A manager who checked your work. His username was PizzaBoss_Dave. I applied. He hired me. First shift, he typed, you put pepperoni on the vegetarian. Redo it. Second shift, he typed, you're late. That was ten seconds. Third shift, he typed, great job today, you earned a bonus. And then, you need to clean your room. I stared at the screen. That's not a Bloxburg thing to say. Then, from downstairs, I heard my dad laugh. I ran down. He was at the kitchen table with his laptop. Bloxburg open. Pizza shop. He'd been playing for a month. My little sister had made him the account. He said he wanted to see what I do all day. And then he got really into the pizza business. I said, you've been my boss for a week. He said, and you've been a pretty bad employee. I said, the vegetarian thing was one time. He said, three times. Now we have a deal. I keep my job at the pizza place, and he doesn't fire me in front of the whole server. But he still makes me work the weekend shift. Would you work for your dad?

title: In Piggy, the bot started typing in chat
caption: Have you ever seen a bot type? (fictional story)
text: I was the last survivor in a Piggy round when the Piggy bot started typing to me in chat. Bots can't type. I know that. I've played Piggy for years. When there aren't enough players, the game puts in a bot. It walks around. It chases you. It doesn't talk. I was hiding in the closet in the house map. Everyone else had been caught. I was waiting for the bot to walk past so I could grab the last key. It stopped. Right outside my closet. And in chat, from the Piggy, a message. I can see you. I laughed, honestly. I thought it was a glitch. Or someone had taken over the bot somehow. I typed back, no you can't. The Piggy typed, top shelf, left side. I looked. The closet had a shelf. Top. Left side. There was a key on it. I'd never noticed it. The last key. The Piggy typed, take it. I took it. I opened the closet door. The Piggy was standing right there. Facing me. It didn't move. I walked around it. Slowly. It turned to watch me. All the way to the exit. I put in the key. The door opened. Right before I escaped, one more message. Thank you for playing with me. Nobody else talks to me. I escaped. The round ended. I checked the player list. There were only two names. Mine. And one called Piggy_Bot. With a friend request. I accepted it. Would you have accepted it?

title: There's a phone in Brookhaven that only rings at 3 a.m.
caption: Would you answer it? (fictional story)
text: There's a phone in Brookhaven that only rings at three a.m., and last night I answered it. I'm not supposed to be awake at three a.m. But I couldn't sleep, so I hopped on Brookhaven. Quiet server. Just me and two other players. I was driving around when I heard it. Ringing. A phone. Not my phone. A phone in the game. I followed the sound. It came from the old phone booth by the gas station. Nobody uses it. Most people don't even know it's clickable. It was ringing. Over and over. I walked up to it. The other two players walked up too. One of them typed, don't. The other typed, answer it, coward. I clicked it. The screen went quiet. All the city sounds stopped. Cars. Music. Everything. Then a message popped up on my screen. Not in chat. In the middle of the screen. Who's there? I typed in chat, me. Another message. Not you. The one behind you. I turned my camera around. The two other players were still there. But now there were three. A third avatar was standing right behind them. All black. No face. No name. I turned back to the phone. One last message. It's been waiting all night for someone to pick up. Thanks. And the screen went normal. Cars. Music. Everything back. And all three of them were gone. Would you have answered the phone?
